title: Succession by generation has never been broken by a world-wide cataclysm

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Succession by generation has never been broken by a world-wide cataclysm

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since all living forms are lineal descendants of forms that lived long before the Silurian epoch, the ordinary succession by generation has never once been broken and no cataclysm has ever desolated the whole world.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As all the living forms of life are the lineal descendants of those which lived long before the Silurian epoch, we may feel certain that the ordinary succession by generation has never once been broken, and that no cataclysm has desolated the whole world.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIV, “Recapitulation and Conclusion”; section “Concluding remarks”. Scope: the history of life on earth

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch14-12: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A worldwide sterilizing cataclysm and broken descent have strong genomic and geological consequences. Existing evidence spans all major lineages and extinction boundaries, though absolute proof of uninterrupted survival is limited by preservation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test genomes of all major living lineages for uninterrupted genealogical continuity from deep ancestors and examine global stratigraphic and extinction records for an interval that eliminated all life. Any independently originated post-cataclysm lineage or truly sterile global break refutes the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Absence of fossils cannot prove absence of survivors.

Pre-Silurian ancestry is inferred from phylogeny rather than direct continuous fossils.

Microbial survival is poorly represented in occurrence databases.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.82
data existence: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Total biotic reboot versus continuity through survivors is detectable in principle, and public occurrence data show survivors across the major Phanerozoic extinctions, none of which is a global end of all lineages. Phylogenies of living groups likewise connect them to pre-Silurian ancestors without a second origin. Precambrian resolution is weaker, but it does not erase the Phanerozoic test the fossil record can already decide.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Search the post-Silurian and earlier fossil record for any interval in which all lineages disappear and later life is phylogenetically unconnected to what came before. The claim is confirmed if every extinction interval retains survivors that include the ancestors of later biotas, and refuted by a global barren gap followed by a biota with no genealogical connection to earlier organisms.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Extinction percentages depend on species concepts and on how completely each interval was sampled.

The claim is a universal negative, so its strength is set by the worst-sampled interval rather than by the well-known mass extinctions.

A complete sterilization in the poorly fossiliferous Precambrian, followed by survival of one lineage, would be difficult to see.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If no cataclysm ever desolated the whole world and the succession by generation was never broken, then at every stage boundary of the Phanerozoic a substantial share of the marine animal genera present must cross into the next stage, and survivors must be found in every major animal phylum even at the worst boundary.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: For each of 96 Phanerozoic stages (two youngest dropped) the fraction of marine animal genera present that are also recorded after the stage (X_bt + X_Ft over all present) was computed from the PBDB diversity table. The stage with the lowest crossing fraction (Stage 4) was identified and the same table was retrieved for nine major lineages to count survivors across that boundary.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Using PBDB occs/diversity stage-level tables for marine Animalia genera (Phanerozoic) and the same table for each of nine marine animal phyla/classes (Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Arthropoda, Echinodermata, Cnidaria, Bryozoa, Porifera, Annelida, Chordata), define for each stage i the boundary-crossing fraction C_i = (X_bt + X_Ft) / (X_bt + X_Ft + X_bL + X_FL), the share of genera present in stage i that are also recorded after it (range-through or first-appearing and continuing). Exclude the two youngest stages (Recent edge). Pass if (1) the minimum C_i over all retained Phanerozoic stage boundaries is >= 0.10 (at no point did fewer than one in ten marine genera survive), AND (2) at the stage with the minimum C_i, at least 7 of the 9 phyla/classes have C_i > 0 (survivors in at least seven major lineages), AND (3) the median C_i over all stages is >= 0.5. Verdict 'supports' if all three hold; 'mixed' if (1) and (2) hold but (3) fails, or if (1) fails only marginally (0.05 <= min C_i < 0.10) while (2) holds; 'refutes' if any boundary has min C_i < 0.05 or fewer than 7 of 9 lineages have survivors at the worst boundary.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Refuted if the fossil record contains a stage boundary across which fewer than 5% of marine animal genera persist, or at which survivors are absent from three or more of the nine major lineages, which would indicate a near-total biotic reset incompatible with unbroken descent. The Precambrian part of the claim ('long before the Silurian') cannot be tested with this data and is excluded from the verdict.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: minimum stage-boundary crossing fraction of marine animal genera (Phanerozoic)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Darwin's 'cataclysm desolating the whole world' is read as an event after which (nearly) no lineages persist, detectable as a stage boundary crossed by very few genera in very few lineages. 'The ordinary succession by generation has never once been broken' is tested only for the Phanerozoic marine record, where stage-level genus ranges exist; the Precambrian ancestry 'long before the Silurian' is outside what occurrence data can show. Boundary-crossing fractions are biased downward by incomplete sampling (Signor-Lipps and Lazarus effects), which makes the test conservative with respect to the claim. Thresholds of 10% and 7/9 lineages are deliberately lenient about mass extinctions, which Darwin did not deny in degree, and strict about total desolation, which he denied.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Paleobiology Database occs/diversity: marine Animalia genus range categories per stage, Phanerozoic

Paleobiology Database occs/diversity for nine marine animal lineages (Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Arthropoda, Echinodermata, Cnidaria, Bryozoa, Porifera, Annelida, Chordata)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Only the Phanerozoic marine record is tested; the claim's Precambrian ancestry statement and terrestrial life are untested.

Boundary-crossing fractions are depressed by incomplete sampling (Signor-Lipps, Lazarus taxa) and by stage boundaries having been drawn at faunal breaks; both biases work against the claim, so a pass is conservative.

Genus-level survival understates species-level loss; Darwin's claim concerns continuity of descent, for which any surviving lineage suffices, so genus level is appropriate.

Stage-level resolution cannot distinguish a single instantaneous event from a protracted crisis within one stage.
